messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: Increased 5xx rate and connection errors observed originating from az1a inference fleet. Auto-threshold triggered at 3387654321. Rolling error rate: 13% (baseline <1%). Latency p50 -> 220ms, p95 -> 1.8s. Affected: hosted text generation routes behind gproxy-az1a. :rotating_light:

maya (oncall): acked. paging PD now. spinning up triage in #incidents. I’m on it.

ops-bot: PD page sent to maya (oncall) and raj (eng-runtime). Incident severity: Sev2 (service degradation). Runbook: `single-az-network-degrade` suggested.

maya (oncall): quick check: health of az1a NLBs? Anyone seeing >50% target failing?

raj (eng-runtime): checking host metrics. Not seeing CPU/GPU OOMs. Network RX/TX counters show spikes and retransmits on a subset of instances. Some host-level ENI errors in CloudWatch: `RxErrors`/`TxErrors` correlated with instance IDs: i-0a1b2c3d4e5f67890.

elaine (sre): looks like ephemeral AZ egress path jitter. DNS resolver latency from az1a also spiking (100s ms). `dig` returns NXDOMAIN intermittently when hitting local resolver pool.

sam (support): any customer-visible symptoms? We have a customer thread reporting increased 500s in inference calls (ticket #INC-19342).

maya (oncall): impact: yes — hosted customers hitting inference API in us-west zone seeing error and retry storms. We should classify affected traffic: hosted API frontends gproxy-usw2 -> regional routing. Might be mostly targeting az1a backing fleet.

raj (eng-runtime): hypothesis: partial zonal capacity degradation due to network path flapping causing connection resets to GPU nodes and causing request retries to accumulate. We can try: 1) shift traffic away from az1a hosts using routing weight; 2) increase connection retries/timeouts on proxy to avoid rapid failover loops; 3) evict worst hosts.

maya (oncall): runbook step 1: enact fast steering: run `trafficctl steer --region=us-west-2 --exclude-az=az1a --dry-run=false` (we have a controlled steering tool). I’ll do that now.

maya (oncall): running `trafficctl steer --region=us-west-2 --exclude-az=az1a --reason \"az1a net errors\"` -> applying. Observed immediate drop in p95 on remaining AZs but backlog on gproxy increased while balancing.

ops-bot: routing change pushed. New weights: az1b:70%, az1c:20%, az1a:10% (draining).

elaine (sre): good. now check K/V cache warms. We may see initial latency blips while caches repopulate. Also watch for kvcache regen errors.

raj (eng-runtime): evicting nodes with repeated ENI errors. Running `fleetctl drain --instances i-0a1b2c3d4e5f67890,i-0b2c3d4e5f6a78901 --reason \"net errors\"`.

maya (oncall): started support comms: posting to customers with impact window estimate. @sam please coordinate CS messages.

sam (support): drafting: \"We’re investigating increased inference errors in us-west. We’ve temporarily routed traffic away from affected AZ and are working on mitigation. No data loss. ETA for stabilization: 15-30m.\" Will send once you approve.

lucy (product): FYI, a few Enterprise customers have long-running Dedicated pools pinned to az1a. We should flag them for follow-up (potential capacity/SLAs).

maya (oncall): note — dedicated capacity pinned to az1a not affected by steering. Need manual outreach. Adding list: cust-omega, cust-horizon.

raj (eng-runtime): mitigation progress: evictions finished for 6 instances, service has fallen back to healthy hosts. Downstream proxies report reduced conn resets. Error rate trending down to ~4%.

ops-bot: autoscale group in az1b triggered +4 g5-inference instances to absorb traffic.

elaine (sre): resolver pool in az1a still flaky; K/V cache regen success rate ~60% for new requests hitting az1a. Recommend keeping weight low until resolver latency normalizes.

maya (oncall): agree. keeping az1a at 5-10% for control and slow drain. I’ll keep the steering active for 1 hour and re-evaluate.

raj (eng-runtime): additional mitigation: enabled proxy-level circuit breaker for routes with >5% errors to reduce retry storms: `gproxy config set circuit_breaker.threshold=5%` -> applied.

sam (support): sent customer advisory to impacted customers. Two customers replied asking for timeline and whether their Dedicated pools are affected. I responded with current mitigation and flagged Dedicated customers to SEs.

lucy (product): raising to sales/SEs: please prepare handoff note for cust-omega + cust-horizon; they need telecon if degradation persists.

maya (oncall): monitoring SLO impact: current 5xx door is 3.8% across region, still above target. No broad data corruption. Marking incident as ‘in progress — partial outage’.

ops-bot: automated note: Collecting logs and certificates for postmortem. Remember to run `incident-collect --thread=3387654321` before cleanup.

elaine (sre): note for follow-up: need to open a ticket with AWS support — ENI Rx drops and resolver backend anomalies in az1a. Likely an underlying host networking path issue. I’ll file SR-99812 and include instance IDs/ENI metrics.

raj (eng-runtime): also we should consider cross-region routing fallback policy in Optimize. For now manual steer is fine but we need an automated fallback for single-AZ THREAT windows. Filed RFC-4648.

maya (oncall): handing off to next oncall at 3387654389. Summary for handoff: detected az1a network-induced connection resets -> steering away from az1a applied -> evicted bad instances -> proxy CB enabled -> customer comms sent -> ongoing: keep az1a weight low, coordinate with AWS SR, follow up with Dedicated customer outreach.

maya (oncall): tagging next oncall: @elaine you’re the lead for follow-up SR and postmortem. @raj continue runtime fixes and bake in routing fallback. @sam continue customer comms.

elaine (sre): on it. I’ll take ownership of the SR and schedule blameless postmortem. I’ll also validate resolver cluster health once SR feedback arrives.

raj (eng-runtime): I’ll instrument more cardinality on ENI error metrics and add a temporary alert for RxError > 3/min across fleet.

sam (support): will follow up with customers listed and provide timeline.

maya (oncall): closing active page. If errors creep back up, re-open with `incident-bot reopen 3387654321`.

ops-bot: Incident update recorded. Severity: Sev2 -> downgraded to Monitoring. Start time: 3387654321. Current error rate: 2.2% (recovering).

maya (oncall): post-incident action items: 1) AWS SR (elaine). 2) Postmortem doc + timeline (elaine + raj) 3) routing automation RFC (raj) 4) Dedicated customer impact review (lucy + sam).

lucy (product): will coordinate Dedicated customer outreach with SEs. Thanks team. :heart:

maya (oncall): thanks all — handing off.
